description: SkyPilot-based multi-cloud LLM deployment — `sky serve up` launches a managed serving endpoint across AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes, auto-picks cheapest region, handles spot preemption, load balances replicas. Ships a vLLM service spec, a sky-serve controller config, and a README flow. For teams running LLM inference across clouds or on spot GPUs without writing Terraform.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick SkyPilot when you want a single YAML that deploys LLM inference across AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes, handles spot preemption + failover, and auto-picks the cheapest region. For single-host docker-compose deployment, use vllm-server / tgi-server / sglang-server directly. SkyPilot is the multi-cloud orchestrator — the underlying server is still vLLM (or whatever you specify).
firstSteps: Configure one cloud — `aws configure` / `gcloud auth login` / `kubectl config` — then `sky check`
Review service.yaml — set resources.accelerators, the model id, and replica count
sky serve status {{endpointName}} — wait for a replica to reach READY, then hit the printed URL
gotchas: SkyPilot provisions real cloud resources. `sky serve up` starts billing immediately — always run `sky serve down {{endpointName}}` when you're done.
Accelerator strings are SkyPilot-specific: `A100:1`, `A100-80GB:1`, `H100:1`. Cloud-specific names (`p4d.24xlarge`) go under `resources.instance_type`.
`use_spot: true` is great for cost but spot preemption will restart replicas; services.yaml `readiness_probe` must be tuned for cold-start time.
First `sky serve up` launches a controller VM (~$30/month on AWS). Reuse it for all services — don't `sky down` the controller.
Model weights download on every replica spawn unless you mount a shared bucket. For large models, use `file_mounts` with S3/GCS to cache weights.
Credentials: SkyPilot reads local cloud SDK configs (~/.aws, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.kube). CI pipelines need these explicitly plumbed.
Kubernetes backend: `sky check kubernetes` must succeed BEFORE `sky serve up` — otherwise SkyPilot silently falls back to the first configured cloud.

placeholders.description: service.yaml (MODEL_ID, accelerators, replica count, spot flag)
sky-serve.yaml (controller sizing, readiness probe, load balancing policy)
HF_TOKEN for gated models — passed into the replicas via the envs map in service.yaml.
